item.description:
New covers: twelve layouts and ten map themes, chosen per category.

  • Ten new cover themes drawn as maps, each piece growing its own terrain: survey sheet, tinted relief, night contours, lake, riso overprint, gridded map, orienteering, embossed cloth, sea chart and isobars. They take their colours from the category’s.
  • Edit Category now sets a category’s colours, theme and layouts separately, with every theme previewed in the colours you’ve picked.
  • Map themes carry a strip of their map down each spine.
  • Covers can now take twelve new layouts: tri-band, pasted label, spine-edge title, monogram, editorial, arched window, justified stack, split, colophon strip, Swiss index, running title and ex libris frame. Some print a piece’s details too: its year, its length and its category.
  • Choose a category’s layouts in Edit Category ▸ Layouts. Pick Any and each piece takes its own; neighbours on a shelf never share one.
  • Existing categories keep the covers they have until you change their layouts. New categories start on Any.
  • Spines pick up their cover’s layout: bands, a strip at the foot, a paper spine or a double rule.
  • Covers are kept between launches, so shelves and grids fill in sooner after opening Scribe.

A better command palette, and two small fixes in the reader.

  • The command palette (⌘K) splits commands from pieces, finds up to 50 pieces as you type and says when there are more, and tells you when nothing matches.
  • The highlight colours stay inside the window when you select text near its right or bottom edge.
  • In PDFs, selecting text near the bottom of the window works properly again. The page counter no longer leaves an invisible strip there.

Footnotes in the margin, embeds you can see, and pull quotes.

  • Footnotes in saved articles sit in the margin beside the line that cites them, and ink in word by word as you reach them. Click a number to find its note.
  • Prefer a clear margin? Settings ▸ Reading ▸ Footnotes in the margin, off, keeps them at the end of the piece and shows each one when you hover its number. On narrow windows they always work this way.
  • Embedded posts, videos and podcasts (X, Bluesky, YouTube, Vimeo, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Substack and more) show as a quiet row that links to the original, instead of vanishing.
  • Pull quotes, the enlarged lines magazines set between paragraphs, now keep their emphasis in the reader. This works for Aeon, Substack, WordPress sites and others that mark them up.
  • Typed section breaks like * * * or ⁂ appear as the reader’s own section break.
  • An article’s subtitle, when the page has one, sits under its title in the reader.
  • The reader’s top bar no longer repeats the percentage read; the margin shows it.
  • All of this applies to articles saved from now on.
